title: Adresse à la nation du Président de la République, Félix Tshisekedi suite à la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à l’est du pays
claim: In his national address, Tshisekedi said he was choosing diplomacy over war, cited the East African Community and Luanda processes, and described the eastern crisis as having displaced more than 200,000 people.
source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with explicit crisis-management choices and dates.
ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own crisis framing and choice set.
contrary_evidence: This concerns conventional-security de-escalation, not nuclear command or arsenal decisions.

title: East Africa leaders agree regional force to quell DR Congo crisis
claim: EAC leaders agreed to send a regional force to the DRC, called for an immediate ceasefire, and said the force would work with DRC military and administrative authorities to stabilise the east.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters-sourced regional diplomacy report with explicit meeting outcomes.
ruler_attribution: Tshisekedi was a direct participant in the summit, but the decision was regional rather than unilateral.
contrary_evidence: This is diplomacy around an inherited conflict, not proof of durable implementation.

title: Congo and Rwanda to begin talks amid tensions over insurgency
claim: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi and Kagame were due to begin talks in Luanda amid the M23 offensive, and that Tshisekedi arrived for a mini tripartite summit on peace.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire content reproduced by Euronews with named leaders, date, and meeting purpose.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's diplomatic conduct and participation.
contrary_evidence: Talks were held amid escalation, so the source does not show success or restraint alone.

title: Rwanda says two soldiers detained in Congo have been released
claim: Congo said two Rwandan soldiers had been detained in its territory as evidence that Rwanda was backing the M23 offensive, and it escalated accusations by alleging disguised special forces in eastern Congo.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced contemporaneous reporting of a bilateral security dispute with direct government claims and denials.
ruler_attribution: This reflects Tshisekedi-era state accusations and security posture, not proof of his personal command choices.
contrary_evidence: Rwanda denied the allegations; the report itself records a disputed attribution.

title: U.N. experts say Rwanda has intervened militarily in eastern Congo
claim: A UN Group of Experts said it had solid evidence that Rwandan troops operated with M23 in Rutshuru between November 2021 and July 2022 and supplied weapons, ammunition, and uniforms.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report summarizing a confidential UN expert finding with specific dates and material support claims.
ruler_attribution: Indirect, but highly relevant to Tshisekedi's conflict environment and proxy-setting.
contrary_evidence: This is evidence about external support to M23, not about Tshisekedi ordering aggression.

title: Analyse du récent rapport d'experts de l'ONU sur la RDC
claim: Radio Okapi reported that the leaked UN expert report accused the Rwandan army of participating in attacks on Congolese soldiers and of equipping and reinforcing M23, while also saying Congolese forces had supported some armed groups in eastern DRC.
source_confidence_reason: Local-language outlet summarizing a confidential UN expert report and the competing allegations it contained.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's public attribution and the conflict setting, but not a personal finding of command responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The report summary includes claims about both sides and remains partly mediated through commentary.

title: Tension RDC-Rwanda : la CEEAC exige le retrait du M23
claim: The CEEAC summit called for the immediate withdrawal of M23 in line with the Nairobi roadmap, and the report notes that Tshisekedi opened the conference in Kinshasa under a heightened security context.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local-language political reporting on regional diplomacy and Tshisekedi's role as host and president in office.
ruler_attribution: Directly about Tshisekedi's hosting and political positioning.
contrary_evidence: The item reflects regional pressure, not a unilateral Congolese initiative.

title: Le président Félix Tshisekedi a reçu l'ancien président kenyan, Uhuru Kenyatta
claim: The presidency said Uhuru Kenyatta was visiting Kinshasa as EAC facilitator for the Nairobi peace process and that the talks were preparing the third round of peace negotiations with armed groups willing to disarm.
source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential communication on an actual meeting and peace-process preparation.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's engagement with the Nairobi process.
contrary_evidence: Official favorable framing; it does not prove battlefield results.

title: Le mini-sommet de Luanda impose au m23/Rwanda un cessez-le-feu et le retrait des zones occupées en RDC
claim: The Luanda mini-summit produced a ceasefire to take effect on 25 November and required M23 to withdraw from occupied areas in the DRC.
source_confidence_reason: Primary presidency communiqué on a dated regional agreement in which Tshisekedi participated.
ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Tshisekedi's participation in a regional settlement effort.
contrary_evidence: Agreement terms do not establish compliance or long-term peace.

title: Troisième phase des pourparlers de Nairobi : Les chefs d’Etats appellent les groupes armés à déposer les armes
claim: Tshisekedi said M23 had to stop hostilities, withdraw from its positions, and return to its November 2021 lines as a condition for joining the Nairobi peace process.
source_confidence_reason: Direct quotation of Tshisekedi in contemporaneous local-language reporting on the Nairobi process.
period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler statement during peace negotiations
ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own public peace-process position.
contrary_evidence: This is a stated condition for talks, not proof that the condition was enforceable.

title: UNHCR deeply concerned by renewed violence displacing thousands in North Kivu, DR Congo
claim: UNHCR said at least 170,000 civilians had been displaced since the November 2021 escalation and warned that women and girls faced sexual violence, extortion, and repeated displacement.
source_confidence_reason: Authoritative humanitarian briefing note with specific displacement and protection figures.
period_fit: Direct 2022 humanitarian context for Tshisekedi's conflict management
ruler_attribution: Indirect conflict context under Tshisekedi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The source describes harm from armed clashes, not direct presidential orders.

title: In eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the surge in violence has driven thousands of displaced people to the outskirts of Goma
claim: The ICRC said clashes in Rutshuru had forced more than 72,000 people to flee in one week and urged all combatants to protect civilians and allow humanitarian workers access.
source_confidence_reason: Primary humanitarian field report from the ICRC with exact displacement figures and IHL framing.
ruler_attribution: Conflict context under Tshisekedi, with implications for state protection duties.
contrary_evidence: This is field reporting on armed clashes, not a finding of presidential culpability.

title: UNHCR gravely concerned by death toll of displaced in DR Congo's east
claim: UNHCR reported over 800 deaths from firearm and machete attacks in Ituri between February and June 2022, including many people sheltering in displacement sites, and said recent fighting in North Kivu had displaced more than 160,000 people.
source_confidence_reason: Authoritative humanitarian briefing with concrete casualty and displacement figures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect inherited-conflict context for Tshisekedi's security decisions.
contrary_evidence: It does not itself separate rebel, local, or government responsibility for each death.

title: Les enfants sous attaque dans l'escalade du conflit à l'est de la RDC
claim: UNICEF said armed attacks in Rutshuru killed four children and that more than 158,000 people, about half children, had been displaced since late March in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF country office press release with exact date and displacement figures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect civilian-harm context under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: This does not assign the attacks to Tshisekedi personally.

title: UNICEF: Mass displacements in eastern DRC pose a deadly threat to children and young people
claim: UNICEF said humanitarian access was becoming more restricted because of the deteriorating security situation, and that fighting between Congolese forces and M23 had intensified since 20 October 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF briefing with a dated statement about access constraints and escalation.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's ability to protect civilians and sustain access.
contrary_evidence: A humanitarian access warning is not a direct finding of commander-level negligence.

title: Facing displacement alone
claim: UNICEF reported that the latest wave of violence had driven 190,000 people from their homes and that many children arrived alone or separated from their families at displacement sites.
source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF field story with a concrete displacement estimate and protection consequence.
ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to the government's civilian-protection record.
contrary_evidence: Story format is illustrative rather than a full incident ledger.

title: Life is tough here
claim: UNICEF described a displaced mother in North Kivu who fled armed conflict and said she lost her husband and agricultural harvest, illustrating the conflict's destructive effect on livelihoods and schooling.
source_confidence_reason: Primary field story, but anecdotal rather than statistical.
ruler_attribution: Context for the social cost of the eastern conflict under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: A single vignette cannot establish national-level responsibility on its own.

title: DR Congo: Resurgent M23 Rebels Target Civilians
claim: Human Rights Watch said M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and expanded control in the east, documenting deliberate civilian harm by the rebels.
source_confidence_reason: Well-documented independent human-rights report based on field reporting and interviews.
ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's security environment and proxy-control problem.
contrary_evidence: The source is about M23 conduct, not direct acts by Tshisekedi.

title: It shouldn’t be happening again: M23 rebels return to wreak havoc in DRC
claim: The article reported that the renewed M23 fighting had again displaced tens of thousands, with by the end of May 72,000 displaced according to the UN, and described the reappearance of old patterns of violence in North Kivu.
source_confidence_reason: Independent field reporting with a clear date and referenced UN displacement estimate.
ruler_attribution: Indirect inherited-conflict context for Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: This is descriptive context, not a direct attribution of policy choice.

title: I prayed to God to find him: the families scattered by violence in DRC
claim: The article said since November 2021 the M23 fighting had killed hundreds and forced nearly 200,000 people from their homes and land, separating families across Rutshuru.
source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with a direct displacement estimate and year-specific conflict timeline.
ruler_attribution: Context for Tshisekedi's conflict-handling choices and civilian-protection record.
contrary_evidence: It is reportorial context, not a legal or official finding.

title: Renewed fighting in DRC raises fears of chaotic proxy conflict
claim: The article said the fighting had displaced at least 400,000 people since March and described the conflict as a regional proxy struggle, with outside support and weak incentives for peace concessions.
source_confidence_reason: Independent synthesis of UN and diplomatic reporting with explicit displacement and proxy-conflict framing.
ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's end-of-year peace and stability posture.
contrary_evidence: This is a synthesis article and mixes reporting with analysis.

title: UN experts: Rwandan forces operate with M23 rebels in Congo
claim: AP reported that UN experts had solid evidence that members of Rwanda's armed forces were operating in eastern Congo in support of M23, which was driving deaths and massive civilian displacement.
source_confidence_reason: AP wire report summarizing a confidential UN expert finding with precise attribution and consequences.
ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's conflict environment and claims about external support.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove Tshisekedi's own conduct; it supports the external-aggression context.

title: Congo crisis in focus at UN General Assembly
claim: At the UN General Assembly, Tshisekedi said Rwanda's involvement and responsibility in the tragedy in areas occupied by the Rwandan army and its M23 allies were no longer questionable.
source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting of a ruler statement at a dated multilateral forum.
ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's public narrative about the conflict.
contrary_evidence: This records Tshisekedi's accusation, not independent proof that the accusation was fully correct.

title: Profonds changements au commandement de l'armée : Tshiwewe a l'état-major général Fardc et Ephraïm Kabi à la garde républicaine
claim: The presidency said Tshisekedi issued ordinances reshuffling the FARDC command, including naming Christian Tshiwewe as chief of staff, as part of military reform.
source_confidence_reason: Primary announcement of personnel changes in the armed forces made under presidential authority.
ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's formal authority over military appointments.
contrary_evidence: A personnel reshuffle does not by itself show better battlefield performance or accountability.

title: La guerre diplomatique et médiatique entre la RDC et le Rwanda s’accélère depuis le drame de Kishishe
claim: Le Monde reported that by late December France, Belgium, Germany, and other chancelleries were publicly denouncing Kigali's support for the M23 after the Kishishe killings.
source_confidence_reason: Independent French-language synthesis of diplomatic reactions to the 2022 conflict escalation.
ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's foreign-relations outcome and international standing.
contrary_evidence: The article is a synthesis and not a primary diplomatic note.
